title: Discharge Management in the Neurological Teaching Hospitals of the University of Oldenburg: An Analysis of Current Practice
summary:
The transition from the hospital to further care at home or in other facilities is a particularly important phase for many patients. If this transition is not well organized, problems can arise, such as missing medical aids, unclear responsibilities, or readmissions to the hospital.
The aim of this study is to examine how the discharge of patients in neurological hospitals is currently organized. In particular, it focuses on which tasks are carried out by the different professional groups and how collaboration between them works.
For the study, staff from medical, nursing, and social service departments in four neurological hospitals will be interviewed. In short, structured conversations, they will describe how the discharge process takes place in everyday work and where they see potential for improvement.
The results are intended to help better understand existing processes and to develop approaches for improving the organization of patient discharge.
conditions: Organization and implementation of discharge management in neurological hospital departments.
